text:
Mark Scheifele became the Jets' all-time leading goal scorer on Saturday against Vegas, passing Dale Hawerchuk, per The Hockey Writers. Winnipeg lost that one in a shootout, then beat Utah 4-2 on Monday to finish an 8-1-1 run over its last 10.

This was supposed to be the year after. The Jets traded Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey on Oct. 23 for Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Nick Bjugstad and picks, and the fallout is still in the headlines, with Hellebuyck saying the threats against his family went beyond online death threats (per Yahoo Sports). Mercer has done his part: 6 points in his last 10 games, and Yahoo Sports says Jets fans have nothing to worry about with him.

At 12-9-4, the record is a little ahead of the play. Winnipeg has 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) on the season and 54% over the last 10, and our standings model has it about three points ahead of its play. Morgan Barron has 9 points in 10 games against 4.3 expected, which won't last. Josh Morrissey's first goal of the season was an overtime winner.

The Scheifele and Kyle Connor line, with either Cole Perfetti or Gabriel Vilardi, takes about 52% of the chances. The penalty kill gives up 0.82 expected goals a game, more than the 0.77 the power play creates. Our playoff odds have the Jets at 33%. What we'd watch: whether the goaltending after Hellebuyck holds up over a full winter.
headline: Scheifele's record, and Jets who keep winning
